title: Audience requests, A-Train and trombone showmanship
summary: He plays mostly requests, closes with a standing-ovation A-Train, uses trombone gimmicks, and arranges Sweet Georgia Brown Basie-style.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: What sort of programs do you play? What sort of music do you play?
I take requests.
Yeah.

Take all requests. Some of them, you got some people want Dixieland (inaudible). Some people like (inaudible). Some of them like Broadway. A lot of them like one o'clock jumps. A lot of guys come in there, smart guys (inaudible) swinging the blues and "I Don't Want to Set the World on Fire," and all that. Then I got a good singer out there with me, a fella, you know. He can sing. (Inaudible) like Tommy Dorsey and the Sheik and he sings all that and he sings Tangerine and Summertime. Everything's always requests. ________ requests. Very seldom do we get a chance to play anything on our own. (Inaudible) into those "I Don't Know Whys", too. (Laughter.)
(Inaudible) does a lot of things. A lot of them won't (inaudible).
: Oh, he's not (inaudible). Why that's popular, I never could understand. I used to --
And one of the things they really rave over is we got is specially on the "A-Train." So, that have to be the last number. That gets the standing ovation.
: Earl Warren always used to play "Harlem Nocturne" on the alto and he used --
Yeah, we got an arrangement on "Sweet Georgia Brown." (Inaudible) was out there once.
: Who?
Rudy.
: Oh, yeah.
And (inaudible).
: How many instruments did he play?
He only played the clarinet.
: Oh, that's -- I tell him you should do with (inaudible), stop fooling around with those saxaphones, you know.
(Inaudible) Henry says, "We got the greatest arrangement" he has ever heard in his life on "Sweet Georgia Brown."
: Yeah?
Yeah.
When did you do that?
Out there.
Oh.
(Inaudible), you know. I do about (inaudible) all the way uptown. I do about 16 miles on the trombone and in the __________ joints and for the introduction and people like that (inaudible), see.
Yeah, well, you've got to have that. I mean, you've got to have some showmanship (inaudible).

I'd like to have (inaudible) like that and the (inaudible) you know, all them things, all the way down the slide, same note, (inaudible) I'm into the melody and it's up, way up. See, that's what they go for (inaudible) terrific solo. We got about three ensembles. Got the drums all mixed up (inaudible) and we do (inaudible) and all like that. They really crazy about that because we do it (inaudible).
Do they?
The way we do it.
Do you like that? I never liked that number particularly.
The way we do it. And most all our stuff is like Basie's, up and down.
Yeah, yeah.
A few minutes, we (inaudible). The next minute, we're all the way up.
